subject: Re: Renewal conversation — EU primary + APAC standby, capacity uplift and term options
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie@wellnesscloud.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: WellnessCloud Procurement <procurement@wellnesscloud.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + region expansion questions (EU primary, APAC standby)

Monica —

Thanks for the helpful call last week. As we start the formal renewal discussion, two items are front-and-center for WellnessCloud:

1) Make EU the primary data residency for EU users (logs + embeddings persisted in-region).
2) Add APAC as a warm-standby region for traffic surge and DR during APAC business hours.

We expect a ~1.8x token volume increase during our next 12 month term due to product expansion in APAC. We want to understand:

- How that uplifts committed capacity pricing for Dedicated/Dedicated+WarmStandby options.
- What term changes / minimum commitments you recommend to get predictable pricing and a failover SLA.
- How KMS/HSM key handling will work across regions (we need in-region key residency for EU primary).

Can you send a rough SOW and an ops runbook for the cutover and the failover behaviour (canary, metrics, rollback)? Procurement will need pricing and a draft SOW to start the internal approval.

Thanks — happy to sync Tuesday morning PT.

— Julie Park
Head of Platform, WellnessCloud

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Julie Park <julie@wellnesscloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, WellnessCloud Procurement <procurement@wellnesscloud.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + region expansion questions (EU primary, APAC standby)

Julie —

Appreciate the clear ask. I attached a draft SOW (WC-SOW-v3.pdf) and a capacity cost workbook that shows both committed and burst models. High level answers below; we can refine numbers after a quick sync with Eng and Finance: 

- Residency: We can make EU the primary residence for all persisted data (embeddings, logs, KV snapshots). KMS integration supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in the EU region only — keys remain in-region.

- APAC warm-standby: We support an APAC standby pool with automated traffic shifting. Standby capacity is billed as reserved warm capacity (discounted) + small cross-region egress margin for failover runs.

- Capacity uplift: For ~1.8x token growth we recommend a 12-month committed uplift with a 20% headroom buffer and staged top-ups at months 3 and 6. I included two pricing scenarios in the workbook: Reserved uplift vs. Reserved + burst.

- Terms: To give Procurement confidence we can offer a 12-month commitment with an optional 3-month extension at a pre-negotiated rate. We can swap to a 24-month term for an extra discount if they want price stability.

Next steps I suggest:
- Internal quick sync (30m) Mon/Tue to lock on preferred pricing structure.
- Engineering to review runbook and validate canary windows — looping in Karthik and Soojin here.
- I’ll send a DocuSign link for the SOW once we agree on the commitment.

If Tuesday PT works, propose 10:30am PT.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0192

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Julie Park <julie@wellnesscloud.com>, WellnessCloud Procurement <procurement@wellnesscloud.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + region expansion questions (EU primary, APAC standby)

Monica / team —

Short engineering note after a quick capacity sketch:

- APAC standby model: recommend a warm-standby pool sized to handle 60% of peak APAC traffic (with auto-burst to on-demand GPUs for full failure scenarios). This keeps steady-state costs lower while giving fast failover.

- Failover behaviour: traffic routing changes are staged:
  * Canary (1% traffic to APAC) for 15 min monitoring latency/error trends;
  * Progressive ramp (1% -> 25% -> 60% over 30 min windows) with automated rollback on error thresholds;
  * KV prefix warming and cache priming pre-ramp to limit cold-start latency.

- SLA/credits: we can commit to a regional failover RTO of 15 minutes (route activation) and provide 10% service credits for missed targets tied to error-rate or route-activation latency. Finance will draft exact credit language; options in SOW.

- Data residency and keys: KMS keys can be customer-managed and bound to EU region. Cross-region failover will use encrypted replication where persisted artifacts remain encrypted and keys do not leave the EU; we will use a short-lived re-encryption key for APAC processing if customer authorizes (documented in the SOW).

Open questions for Procurement:
- Are they comfortable with a warm-standby sizing at 60% of peak vs. a fully reserved 100% approach?
- Do they require a firm RTO in the contract or prefer operational runbook + weekend drills?

I can join the Tue 10:30am PT call to walk the runbook.

— Karthik
Director, Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Julie Park <julie@wellnesscloud.com>, WellnessCloud Procurement <procurement@wellnesscloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + region expansion questions (EU primary, APAC standby)

Julie —

Thanks — great sync earlier. Per our call I’ve: 

- Attached the updated SOW (WC-SOW-v3.pdf) with two commercial options (12m committed uplift vs 24m committed for additional discount).
- Attached the security question workbook and the capacity-cost breakdown.
- Drafted the runbook summary into section 4 of the SOW (canary cadence, metrics for rollback, KV priming steps).

Action items / timeline:
- Procurement: review pricing options and confirm preferred commitment (12m or 24m) by EOD Thu 4/16 so we can get DocuSign out next week.
- Engineering (Karthik/Soojin): proposal to run a cross-region drill during the pilot window (target week of 5/10). Please confirm feasibility by Wed 4/15.
- I will open the DocuSign envelope once Procurement locks commitment and draft minor term language around RTO and Service Credits.

If Procurement wants to change the warm-standby sizing we can update the workbook and show the cost delta. Happy to walk Procurement through the numbers on Thursday morning PT — let me know a preferred time.

Thanks again — attaching links: DocuSign (https://www.docusign.com/transaction/abcdef123456) and HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/WC-2026-0421).

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0192
